name: Talking portraits
oneLiner: Portraits animated by the dialogue: a typewriter that owns the line (or follows the game's own), a mouth that moves only while a letter is typed and shuts on spaces, punctuation, pauses and when the line ends, seeded random blinks, 1 px idle breathing, and an emotion tag per line (or inside it) that changes the face through a short blink-through with a 1 px posture beat, never a one-frame jump. Faces are code-drawn 16-bit busts from the D-04 generator (expressive-portraits.js, used through its API) or the game's own portrait through a draw callback; the speaker's framed panel sits in the game's dialogue box with a name plate, and any face can sit in a HUD and react to hits.
fits: RPGs and adventures with dialogue boxes (villagers, quest givers, cutscenes)
turn-based battles that want battle barks and faces that wince when hit
party HUDs and status screens with living faces
notFor: voice-acted games that need lip sync to audio (the mouth follows the typed text, not phonemes)
HD painted portraits (D-04 faces are 16-bit pixel art; a painted portrait can still use the draw callback if it has mouth and eye frames)

needs: every place the game sets a dialogue or message line (open and each advance) and where it closes
the confirm key / tap handler (a press first finishes a typing line)
a fixed update step, also while the dialogue pauses the game (also the ?t= fast-forward)
the dialogue box rect in native px, drawn by the game; the game's own text drawing
a cast: a D-04 portrait spec or a draw callback per speaking character; expressive-portraits.js loaded first for specs
provides: the speaker's framed portrait inside the dialogue box and a name plate, with the text rect beside it (drawSpeaker -> layout)
the typed text as rows wrapped on the full line (no word jumps)
press() that finishes a typing line before the game advances
faces anywhere with drawFace, react(name, emotion, ms) for hits and wins
follow(text, shown) for games that keep their own typewriter
state() per face (emotion, eyes, mouth, transition) for tests

assets: module/talking-portraits.js: the element as one dependency-free script (global GameDNA_TalkingPortraits): typewriter with punctuation holds, mouth sync, blinks, breathing, emotion transitions, the speaker panel and name plate (5x7 caps built in), faces for HUDs
faces from elements/expressive-portraits/module/expressive-portraits.js (D-04), used through make() / draw() only; no image files
demo only: pixel-kit tavern room and actors, C-03 pixel-font for the dialogue text
